Which two nuclei are isotopes of the same element?
A
P and Q
B
P and S
C

D
R and S

hints: Notice the table gives number of neutrons and nucleon number $A$, not proton number directly, so you must find proton number $Z$ first.
Recall isotopes have the same proton number $Z$ with different neutron numbers, where $Z = \text{nucleon number} - \text{number of neutrons}$.
Calculate $A-N$ for P, Q, R and S and look for the pair with the same $Z$ but different $N$.
walkthrough: Isotopes are nuclei of the same element, so they must have the same number of protons $Z$ but different numbers of neutrons.
Use $\text{nucleon number } A = Z + N$, rearranged to $Z = A - N$, for each nucleus in the table.
Compare proton numbers: only R and S share $Z = 8$, while their neutron numbers $6$ and $8$ differ, giving different nucleon numbers $14$ and $16$.
Same $Z$ with different $N$ satisfies the definition of isotopes. This is option D.

A.explanation: P has proton number $10-5=5$ and Q has $10-6=4$, so different proton numbers mean different elements.

B.explanation: P has proton number $5$ and S has $16-8=8$, so they cannot be the same element.

C.explanation: Q and R both have 6 neutrons, but Q has proton number $4$ and R has $14-6=8$, so equal neutrons does not make isotopes.

D.explanation: R and S both have proton number $8$ with different neutron numbers, $6$ and $8$, so they are isotopes of the same element.
